t:
(a) In General.—The Secretary shall carry out research, development, demonstration, and commercial application programs in fossil energy, including activities under this subtitle, with the goal of improving the efficiency, effectiveness, and environmental performance of fossil energy production, upgrading, conversion, and consumption. Such programs take into consideration the following objectives: 
        (1) Increasing the energy conversion efficiency of all forms of fossil energy through improved technologies.  
        (2) Decreasing the cost of all fossil energy production, generation, and delivery.  
        (3) Promoting diversity of energy supply.  
        (4) Decreasing the dependence of the United States on foreign energy supplies.  
        (5) Improving United States energy security.  
        (6) Decreasing the environmental impact of energy-related activities.  
        (7) Increasing the export of fossil energy-related equipment, technology, and services from the United States.   
    (b) Authorization of Appropriations.—There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out fossil energy research, development, demonstration, and commercial application activities, including activities authorized under this subtitle—
        (1) $611,000,000 for fiscal year 2007;  
        (2) $626,000,000 for fiscal year 2008; and  
        (3) $641,000,000 for fiscal year 2009.   
    (c) Allocations.—From amounts authorized under subsection (a), the following sums are authorized: 
        (1) For activities under section 962—
            (A) $367,000,000 for fiscal year 2007;  
            (B) $376,000,000 for fiscal year 2008; and  
            (C) $394,000,000 for fiscal year 2009.   
        (2) For activities under section 964—
            (A) $20,000,000 for fiscal year 2007;  
            (B) $25,000,000 for fiscal year 2008; and  
            (C) $30,000,000 for fiscal year 2009.   
        (3) For activities under section 966—
            (A) $1,500,000 for fiscal year 2007; and  
            (B) $450,000 for each of fiscal years 2008 and 2009.   
        (4) For the Office of Arctic Energy under section 3197 of the Floyd D. Spence National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2001 (42 U.S.C. 7144d) $25,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2007 through 2009.   
    (d) Extended Authorization.—There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary for the Office of Arctic Energy established under section 3197 of the Floyd D. Spence National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2001 (42 U.S.C. 7144d) $25,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2010 through 2012.  
    (e) Limitations.—
        (1) Uses.—None of the funds authorized under this section may be used for Fossil Energy Environmental Restoration or Import/Export Authorization.  
        (2) Institutions of higher education.—Of the funds authorized under subsection (c)(2), not less than 20 percent of the funds appropriated for each fiscal year shall be dedicated to research and development carried out at institutions of higher education.

fable.w: The section directs the Secretary to run fossil energy research and development programs, lists objectives, and authorizes and allocates appropriations. The tempting reading is that the mention of institutions of higher education brings outside parties in, but they are only recipients of research funding, not parties consulted before a federal decision. Nothing in the section requires rulemaking, public comment, a hearing, an advisory body, consultation with non-federal entities, or a right to sue.
fable.s: not less than 20 percent of the funds appropriated for each fiscal year shall be dedicated to research and development carried out at institutions of higher education.

opus.w: The section only sets out goals for a research program, authorizes appropriations, and divides up and limits the funding. The mention of institutions of higher education is tempting, but it only reserves money for research done there. That is funding, not a chance to weigh in on a federal decision. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a way to challenge a decision.
opus.s: Of the funds authorized under subsection (c)(2), not less than 20 percent of the funds appropriated for each fiscal year shall be dedicated to research and development carried out at institutions of higher education.
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is that the requirement to dedicate funds to research "carried out at institutions of higher education" brings outside parties into the program. It doesn't fit the definition. That clause decides where money goes and who does the research. It gives universities no role in any federal decision. Getting funding is like a grant or contract, which the definition excludes. Nothing else in the section calls for consultation, a hearing, a comment period, rulemaking, an advisory body, or a right to sue.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section outlines internal agency goals, appropriation amounts, and funding limitations. While subsection (e)(2) requires that a portion of funds be dedicated to research at institutions of higher education, this is a grant/contract funding allocation, not a requirement for consultation or coordination with those institutions in the decision-making process. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and there is no mention of advisory boards, public hearings, or consultation with outside parties.
qwen_chat.s:
(e) Limitations.—
        (1) Uses.—None of the funds authorized under this section may be used for Fossil Energy Environmental Restoration or Import/Export Authorization.  
        (2) Institutions of higher education.—Of the funds authorized under subsection (c)(2), not less than 20 percent of the funds appropriated for each fiscal year shall be dedicated to research and development carried out at institutions of higher education.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that requiring funds to be dedicated to "institutions of higher education" (subsection (e)(2)) constitutes participation because it involves outside entities. However, this is a funding allocation constraint for grants or contracts, not a requirement for consultation, coordination, or advisory input from those institutions in the decision-making process. The definition explicitly excludes applications for grants. The rest of the section deals with internal agency goals, appropriations, and internal allocations.
